title: command history
name: Command history
rule: Keep a visible record of what was done, to what, and when, as the user performs actions.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Command History (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A visible record shows what was done, to what, and when.
fail_when: No visible history of what / to what / when.
overview: A visible record of what was done, to what, and when.
apply_when: People need to review or audit recent actions in the product.
not_when: Trivial one-off taps that never need a recoverable history trail.
agent_hint: Keep a visible history of what, to what, and when for user actions.
description: A command history makes past work inspectable: what ran, on which target, and when. Without a visible record, people cannot verify, audit, or reconstruct what happened after a busy session. Provide that trail as actions accumulate so the sequence stays reviewable. Reserve history for meaningful operations; do not invent history UI for fleeting chrome taps that never matter later.
